name: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)
description: The interface segregation principle, or ISP, states that no code should be forced to depend on methods it does not use. It is the ``I`` in the SOLID principles of object-oriented design, and it recommends splitting large, general-purpose interfaces into smaller, more specific ones, so that implementing classes only need to know about the methods that are actually relevant to them. Violating ISP typically shows up as ``fat`` interfaces, where implementers are forced to provide empty or throwing stubs for methods they don't need, which increases coupling and makes the codebase harder to maintain and extend.
